_comment: D1 (2026-08-05): the 29th matrix row, and the ONLY configuration in the tree that exercises the ENABLE_DEBUG RTL arm. Castalia defaults plus core-side debug mode: dcsr/dpc/dscratch0/dscratch1 at 0x7B0-0x7B3 (legal ONLY in debug mode -- from M or U they still raise illegal-instruction), the DRET encoding, an unmaskable halt request sampled at the fourteen FSM recognition points (the thirteen an interrupt uses PLUS the terminal TRAP_STATE, so a debugger can rescue a wedged hart), the parked-hart clock ungate that makes harts 1..N-1 reachable at all, halt-on-reset, ebreak-to-debug under dcsr.ebreakm, and single-step. priv.trapCsr is INHERITED from the schema default (true) rather than named, and the debug=>trapCsr validator would raise if it were not: ebreak and the whole SYSTEM PRIV decode arm are trapCsr-gated. NOTHING DRIVES THE DEBUG PORTS AT CHIP LEVEL -- the Debug Module is D2's -- so on this row the three hart_tile dbg_* ports sit at their '0' entity defaults and a testbench force (xcelium/riscv_test/behavioral_mp/xrun_dbg.sh) is the only way to raise a halt request. The suite therefore behaves exactly as on the default row EXCEPT for what dbgdenymp.S observes: the 0x7Bx block and DRET are still illegal from M-mode, and nothing may reach 0xBE00 unasked. Prove with: SUITE=full make verify CONFIG=config/castalia_debug.json
